full_text_en:
Shanghai Power Supply Bureau v. Proteus Shipping Co., S.A., Panama

Maritime Damage Compensation Dispute

Plaintiff: Shanghai Power Supply Bureau.

Legal Representative: Xue Zhongsu, Director of Shanghai Power Supply Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Xu Jingqian, Director of the Cable Engineering Department of Shanghai Power Supply Bureau.

Agent ad litem: Fang Fenggang, Lawyer of Shanghai No. 1 Law Firm.

Defendant: Proteus Shipping Co., S.A., Panama.

Agent ad litem: Tang Yilin, Lawyer of Shanghai International Economic and Trade Law Firm.

At 15:10 on November 22, 1984, the vessel "M.V. AGAMEMNON," owned by the Defendant, weighed anchor from buoys No. 34-35 on the Huangpu River in Shanghai Port and proceeded at slow speed towards buoys No. 73-74. Because the vessel was sailing with its anchor dragging, when it passed buoy No. 70, the duty officer at the Plaintiff's submarine cable watch station observed that the vessel's port anchor was in the water. The duty officer immediately turned on a neon warning sign marked "CABLE AREA" to give a warning and continuously hailed the vessel through a loudspeaker, requesting it to retrieve the anchor. However, the vessel did not respond and continued sailing with the anchor dragging. Consequently, at 16:52, the port anchor hooked and broke the "Nanpu 383" submarine river-crossing cable laid between buoys No. 72-73. This caused the power supply substation and high-voltage division under the Shanghai Power Supply Bureau, as well as Unit No. 7 generator set of the Nanshi Power Plant, to be disconnected from the power grid, resulting in a power outage in parts of the surrounding area and the shutdown of fourteen factories.

On November 23, the Shanghai Power Supply Bureau applied to the Shanghai Maritime Court for pre-litigation preservation, alleging: The "M.V. AGAMEMNON," owned by Proteus Shipping Co., S.A., Panama, while sailing with its anchor dragging in the Huangpu River, hooked and broke the river-crossing cable between buoys No. 72-73, causing losses to the applicant's equipment, losses from the power supply interruption, and losses sustained by users due to the power outage, totaling RMB 300,000. The applicant requested that the court order the Defendant to provide a bank guarantee, failing which the "M.V. AGAMEMNON" should be detained. On the same day, the Shanghai Maritime Court accepted the pre-litigation preservation application and notified the applicant to provide relevant evidence. On November 26, the court ruled that the Respondent must, within five days of receiving the ruling, provide a guarantee equivalent to RMB 300,000 through either the Bank of China or the People's Insurance Company of China; that the "M.V. AGAMEMNON" must not leave Shanghai Port of the People's Republic of China before the Respondent provided such guarantee; and that if the Respondent failed to provide the guarantee, the "M.V. AGAMEMNON," owned by the Respondent, would be detained according to law. On November 27, the Shanghai Branch of the People's Insurance Company of China, upon authorization, provided the guarantee on behalf of the Respondent's shipowner. On the same day, the Shanghai Power Supply Bureau filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai Maritime Court, demanding that Proteus Shipping Co., S.A., Panama, compensate economic losses totaling RMB 330,023.46.

The Defendant argued in its defense: "Regarding the fact that the 'M.V. AGAMEMNON' shifted berth with its anchor dragging and hooked and broke the cable, the plaintiff's claim is based on presumed fault on the part of the ship, as it has failed to provide conclusive evidence of fault."

After accepting the case, the Shanghai Maritime Court found through investigation: The fact that the "M.V. AGAMEMNON," while sailing with its anchor dragging, hooked and broke the Plaintiff's "Nanpu 383" submarine river-crossing cable was substantiated by the physical evidence of cable remnants found entangled on the vessel's port anchor; by the testimonies of the pilot, the cable watchman, and witnesses to the incident; by the vessel movement records of the Harbor Superintendency Administration and the inspection report of the vessel by the ship inspection authority; by the loss reports from fourteen factories, including Shanghai No. 3 Cold-Rolled Steel Strip Plant, and from Nanshi Power Plant, the Plaintiff's High Voltage Division, and Pudong Power Supply Substation; and by the videotape showing the extent of damage to the "Nanpu 383" cable and the emergency repair work. The fifty-three pieces of evidence obtained during the investigation all proved the tort liability of the "M.V. AGAMEMNON" for hooking and breaking the cable with its port anchor. The Defendant's argument that the Plaintiff's complaint was "based on presumed fault" was unfounded. Based on the above facts, on March 13, 1985, the Shanghai Maritime Court convened the Plaintiff and Defendant for mediation. As the parties disagreed on the amount of damages, mediation failed.

On May 29, 1985, the Shanghai Maritime Court held a public hearing of the case. Through the trial, the court held that the conduct of the "M.V. AGAMEMNON," owned by the Defendant, in sailing with its anchor dragging in the Huangpu River, causing damage to the "Nanpu 383" river-crossing cable laid by the Plaintiff, violated Article 10 of the Maritime Traffic Safety Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 37 of the Shanghai Port Regulations, which prohibit anchoring within 100 meters above or below the cable area. The Defendant should therefore compensate for all economic losses caused. Regarding the amount of compensation, upon verification, the court found that the claims made by the Plaintiff were not entirely reasonable. The court determined the following losses: repair costs for the "Nanpu 383" submarine river-crossing cable totaling RMB 43,618.75 for construction machinery and tools, RMB 40,068.00 for construction labor, RMB 68,844.54 for construction materials, and RMB 35,147.53 for management fees; economic losses of RMB 2,419.82 incurred by the Plaintiff's affiliated Power Supply Substation and High Voltage Division due to equipment damage, totaling RMB 190,098.64. The losses incurred by Shanghai Nanshi Power Plant and the other fourteen factories due to equipment repairs, raw materials, and lost profits amounted to RMB 40,166.22. The total of the above amounts was RMB 230,264.88.

Accordingly, on June 19, 1985, the Shanghai Maritime Court, in accordance with Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), rendered the following judgment:

1.  The Defendant, Proteus Shipping Co., S.A., Panama, shall pay the Plaintiff compensation for economic losses in the amount of RMB 230,264.88.
2.  The remaining claim of the Plaintiff, Shanghai Power Supply Bureau, for RMB 99,758.58, is not supported.
3.  The litigation costs of this case amount to RMB 8,092.53, of which RMB 6,097.36 shall be borne by the Defendant and RMB 1,995.17 shall be borne by the Plaintiff.

On March 3, 1986, the 246th Session of the Adjudication Committee of the Supreme People's Court, pursuant to the provisions of Article 11, Paragraph 1 of the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, while summarizing trial experience, considered that in trying this case, the Shanghai Maritime Court had promptly investigated the facts of the dispute and clarified the parties' respective liabilities; the handling of the compensation amount was pragmatic, fair, and reasonable. In this way, it had protected the legitimate rights and interests of the foreign party while safeguarding the legitimate interests of the domestic party. This case may serve as a reference for people's courts at all levels.
